snippet.title: Shining Force III (Saturn) Playthrough [1 of 3]
snippet.description:
A playthrough of Sega's 1998 strategy-RPG for the Sega Saturn, Shining Force III.

This is the first part of a three-part playthrough. The other parts can be found at:
Part 2: https://youtu.be/lxAoyO-gOoI
Part 3: https://youtu.be/QXOo3_eBfxw

In this video:
4:07  Chapter 1 "Nightmare in the Floating City of Saraband"
2:52:52  Chapter 2 "Cross-Continental Railway"
5:49:44  Chapter 3 "Target: Guardian Statue of Elbesem"

Shining Force III was the penultimate North American release for the Sega Saturn. It followed four years after Shining Force II's 1994 release on the Sega Genesis, and it was the last of the Shining games to be made by Camelot.

Shining Force III is a localization of Shining Force III Scenario 1: Outo no Kyoshin (シャイニングフォースIIIシナリオ1「王都の巨神」, lit. "The Royal Capital's Giant"). Because of its massive scope, SF3 was split up into three parts, but only the first of them was officially released outside of Japan. (Scenarios 2 & 3 have since been translated by fans and made playable on original Saturn hardware.)

In Scenario 1, you play as Synbios, a noble who finds himself leading his forces to war after peace talks between the nations of Aspinia and Destonia break down during a conference in the city of Saraband.

Built on the strong foundation laid by the previous Shining Force titles, SF3 feels incredibly familiar, but it offers several improvements. The battlefields feature dynamic elements that can shake up conditions mid-battle, a friendship system has been implemented, characters can unlock abilities and spells as their skill improves with certain weapon types, the story is far more complex and political in nature than anything seen in the previous games, the JRPG-style exploration segments have been fleshed out, and everything is now presented in 3D.

It strikes the perfect balance between old and new. The systems are about as straightforward as they were in the 16-bit titles, and the nuances introduced by the new mechanics help to keep the game fresh and challenging without sacrificing accessibility. The modernized graphics are flashy, impressive, and greatly improve the readability of the battlefield. The expanded scope of the plot and the creativity shown in the set-pieces make for a more substantial and engaging experience overall. The only major drawbacks are how often the characters drone on and on without saying anything meaningful, and how harsh the attack animations can be on the eyes. (If you have photosensitivity issues, you might want to pass on this one. The rapid, high contrast strobing effects become increasingly intense as the game goes on.)

Shining Force III perfects the series' formula, and though it's a real shame that only the first scenario made its way westward, it still offers a ton of quality gameplay that'll keep you hooked for a long while. 
_____________
No cheats were used during the recording of this video.
